label: first g/u/3 input in original phase after an m/w/z/o/x-heavy prefix
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit: 95% of activation mass is at t < L, peaking at t=2-4, and it never fires at t=0. The input token is the strongest cue. g (9.3x lift, 34% of mass), u (5.7x), and 3 (4.0x) dominate, with weaker contributions from b, p, j, and h. Activations are mostly on the first occurrence of the token (in_first=1 holds 91% of mass). Whether it fires depends on the prefix: it is strongest when earlier inputs include tokens such as m, w, z, o, x, t, or 0, e.g. the top examples are w w m m [3], m w z [g], m o o [g]. The same g/u/3 tokens at t=0 or after other prefixes usually do not fire. The copy phase holds about 5% of mass, almost all at recall_idx=1 (the step after the first output). It is essentially silent at the delimiter and in later copy steps. The predicate only partly captures this. Input-token identity alone gives about 0.58 recall at 0.11 precision. Adding the prefix condition raises precision to about 0.27 at 0.36 recall (dev F1 0.30, mass recall 0.48). This suggests the unit reads out a distributed function of the hidden state that no simple token-set rule reproduces. Coverage is higher for the strongest activations (top quartile), and I did not confirm any other magnitude claims.
